passage.title: A Perfect Attendance Record with a Hidden Cost

paragraphs.text: A bright certificate hung outside the fictional Westbrook School office: one class had achieved perfect attendance for a month. The display celebrated a result the school had worked hard to improve. Transport problems and repeated unexplained absences had previously interrupted lessons, and staff wanted pupils to benefit from being present. Yet the certificate prompted a school nurse to ask another question. Did the record show that pupils had gained better access to learning, or could it also include days when children had attended despite being too unwell to participate comfortably?

The attendance campaign had combined several measures. Staff contacted families to understand recurring difficulties, helped resolve a bus scheduling problem, and introduced awards for classes with no absences. The first measures addressed barriers; the award attached recognition to an outcome. All could affect the same attendance total through different routes. When the total improved, the school could not determine from that number alone which measure had mattered most. Nor did a child being physically present establish how much learning had occurred during the day.

Staff began recording reasons for absence more consistently and comparing them with visits to the nurse and requests to go home early. Previously, the main report had grouped many absences together. The revised records distinguished transport difficulties, reported illness, and reasons that remained unknown. These categories were imperfect because families varied in what they reported, but they made some differences visible. A decrease in transport-related absence suggested a different kind of improvement from a decrease in recorded illness absence accompanied by more pupils becoming unwell at school.

Family conversations supplied another piece of evidence. In the fictional school's review, some parents said their children worried about losing the class award by staying home. That concern could influence a decision even when the school had issued guidance about illness. Other families described the improved bus service as the reason attendance had become easier. The accounts indicated different mechanisms rather than proving that every attending child had felt pressure. They also showed why a single favorable total could combine a useful removal of barriers with a less desirable incentive.

The distinction mattered beyond academic scores. A child who felt ill might be present but unable to engage fully, and some infectious illnesses could affect other pupils and staff. Decisions about staying home needed to follow appropriate health guidance, not a desire to protect an unbroken record. At the same time, an unexplained absence might signal a difficulty for which a family needed help. Treating all absence as failure would obscure both situations. Treating attendance as unimportant would obscure the value of reliable access to lessons.

The school revised the award while keeping the work on barriers. Classes were recognized for collective learning activities that did not require every child to have an unbroken attendance record. Staff continued following recurring absences, examined whether pupils could participate when present, and reviewed illness-related patterns with the health team. They compared similar parts of the year because seasonal illness could otherwise distort the picture. Even then, an improvement could not automatically be attributed to the new award policy alone: transport support and other school conditions had also changed. The staff documented those parallel changes so later readers could assess the comparison.

The certificate remained in a folder as a record of what the school had once chosen to celebrate. The review did not establish that encouraging attendance was harmful, or that the award had caused every illness-related visit. It established that the headline figure was too narrow to carry the school's full claim of improvement. A more informative assessment asked whether barriers had fallen, whether health decisions remained appropriate, and whether time at school supported participation. Westbrook could still value attendance strongly while recognizing that a missing day and a lost learning opportunity were not always the same thing.

questions.stem: How did bus support and the attendance award differ in their possible effects?
questions.stem_ja: バスの支援と出席の表彰では、考えられる効果がどのように異なっていたか。

choices.text: Bus support primarily changed learning quality, whereas the award changed transport reliability.
choices.text_ja: バスの支援は主に学びの質を変え、表彰は通学手段の信頼性を変えた。

choices.text: Bus support helped individuals, whereas the award provided evidence of every pupil's benefit.
choices.text_ja: バスの支援は個人を助け、表彰はすべての生徒が恩恵を受けたことの証拠となった。

choices.text: Bus support affected reported reasons, whereas the award affected actual presence.
choices.text_ja: バスの支援は届け出られる理由に影響し、表彰は実際の出席に影響した。

choices.text: Bus support removed a practical barrier, whereas the award could alter choices about attending.
choices.text_ja: バスの支援は実際的な障壁を取り除き、表彰は登校するかどうかの選択を変えうるものだった。

questions.stem: Which pattern would make a fall in illness-related absence less clearly positive?
questions.stem_ja: どのような傾向があれば、病気による欠席の減少が明らかに好ましいとは言いにくくなるか。

choices.text: Similar total absences in two comparable parts of the school year.
choices.text_ja: 学年のうち比較可能な二つの時期で、欠席の合計数が同程度であること。

choices.text: Fewer unexplained absences following more consistent record keeping.
choices.text_ja: より一貫した記録をとるようになった後、理由の分からない欠席が減ったこと。

choices.text: More families providing specific reasons for transport difficulties.
choices.text_ja: 通学手段の問題について具体的な理由を伝える家庭が増えたこと。

choices.text: More pupils reporting to the nurse while recorded illness absence declined.
choices.text_ja: 記録上の病気による欠席が減る一方で、保健室に来る生徒が増えたこと。

questions.stem: What do the parent conversations establish?
questions.stem_ja: 保護者との話し合いから立証されることは何か。

choices.text: Some families described different reasons for the attendance change.
choices.text_ja: 出席の変化について、家庭によって異なる理由が語られたこと。

choices.text: The class award had more influence than transport support across the school.
choices.text_ja: 学校全体で、クラスの表彰が通学支援よりも大きな影響を与えたこと。

choices.text: Children whose parents mentioned the award had attended while infectious.
choices.text_ja: 保護者が表彰について言及した子どもたちは、感染力のある状態で登校していたこと。

choices.text: Published health guidance had little effect on decisions in most households.
choices.text_ja: 公表された健康上の指針は、ほとんどの家庭で判断にあまり影響を与えなかったこと。

questions.stem: Which approach best preserves the purpose of attendance support?
questions.stem_ja: 出席支援の目的を最もよく保つのは、どの方法か。

choices.text: Reward every reduction in absence after checking that academic scores have increased.
choices.text_ja: 学業成績が上がったことを確認した上で、欠席が減ったらそのすべてを表彰する。

choices.text: Reduce access barriers and assess participation without rewarding attendance that conflicts with health guidance.
choices.text_ja: 参加を妨げる障壁を減らし、健康上の指針に反する出席を表彰することなく、授業への参加状況を評価する。

choices.text: Use illness-related absence as the main target because it affects the attendance total.
choices.text_ja: 病気による欠席は出席の合計数に影響するので、それを主な目標とする。

choices.text: Treat early departures as completed attendance days when reporting the campaign.
choices.text_ja: 取り組みの報告では、早退した日も出席を果たした日として扱う。

questions.stem: Why can a later improvement not be attributed to the revised award alone?
questions.stem_ja: 後の改善を、見直された表彰だけのおかげとみなせないのはなぜか。

choices.text: The school replaced attendance with a measure unrelated to learning.
choices.text_ja: 学校が出席を、学びとは無関係な指標に置き換えたから。

choices.text: An award policy can affect reported reasons but cannot affect behavior.
choices.text_ja: 表彰の方針は届け出られる理由には影響しうるが、行動には影響しえないから。

choices.text: Other interventions and conditions could also have contributed to the result.
choices.text_ja: 他の取り組みや状況も、その結果に寄与した可能性があるから。

choices.text: Seasonal comparison removes the evidence needed to assess the award.
choices.text_ja: 季節をそろえた比較によって、表彰を評価するのに必要な証拠が失われるから。

passage.title: The Frog That Moved Uphill

paragraphs.text: An old map of a mountain shows frog records mainly on lower slopes; a newer map places many records higher up. Consider this hypothetical comparison as a way to examine a real scientific question: what would justify saying that a species had moved uphill? The maps show where observers reported frogs at different times. They do not yet distinguish changes in the animals' distribution from changes in the places and conditions under which people looked. Nor do they reveal whether temperature, breeding habitat, or several influences together explain the apparent shift.

The earliest records might have come from visits to accessible ponds near a road. Later surveys might have reached additional ponds higher on the mountain. If so, some high records could represent newly observed populations rather than newly established ones. A blank area on the older map would mean no recorded observation, which is not necessarily the same as confirmed absence. Before interpreting a trend, investigators would need information about the earlier searches: their locations, timing, methods, and frequency. The history of observation belongs in the comparison alongside the history of the frogs.

Suppose comparable surveys then confirmed that occupancy had declined at some lower sites and increased at higher ones. Rising temperature would be a plausible influence to investigate. Conditions associated with elevation can matter to animals, and warming can change the suitability of a location. Yet this explanation would need more than a broad temperature trend and a matching direction on the map. It would be useful to examine conditions at the occupied and abandoned sites, and to ask whether the expected relationship appeared where other important habitat features were similar.

For a pond-breeding frog, the availability of water through the relevant stages of reproduction is another important condition. A cooler site without a suitable pond may offer little opportunity to establish a breeding population. Changes in rainfall, drainage, or vegetation can alter the moisture and breeding conditions associated with a location. Some of these changes may themselves connect to climate, while others may arise from local activity. Treating temperature and habitat as completely separate competing explanations could therefore be misleading. Warming might affect distribution partly through its relationship with water conditions, rather than through temperature alone.

The time at which observers search also matters. Frogs can be easier to detect during some weather and breeding conditions than others. A single unsuccessful visit provides weaker evidence of absence than repeated suitable searches, although repeated visits still require careful interpretation. If recent surveys occur more often during favorable detection conditions, they may produce more records without an equivalent increase in animals. Researchers can document these conditions and use repeated observations to account for imperfect detection. Such work strengthens the maps as evidence rather than dismissing observations merely because they contain uncertainty.

An informative follow-up would therefore revisit sites across the mountain, record comparable search effort, and track pond conditions along with local temperature and moisture. Evidence of breeding would answer a different question from a sighting of an individual passing through. The results might support several contributions: genuine loss of lower breeding sites, occupation of suitable higher sites, and improved detection in previously poorly surveyed areas. These contributions need not be forced into a single percentage before the basic distinctions are recognized. Identifying them helps show what further evidence would narrow the explanation.

The two maps would then tell a more careful story than their changing dots first suggested. An upward shift could be real, yet its explanation might involve temperature, water, habitat availability, and the observation process together. The conclusion would apply to the studied species and mountain under the examined conditions. It would not establish that all amphibians are moving uphill or that every higher site offers refuge. Understanding the shift requires following the conditions that support a population, as well as the methods that make that population visible to the people drawing its map.

questions.stem: Why might new records at higher sites fail to demonstrate recent colonization?
questions.stem_ja: 高い場所での新しい記録が、最近になって住みついたことを示さない可能性があるのはなぜか。

choices.text: The expanded survey area can establish the direction of movement before differences in search effort are checked.
choices.text_ja: 調査範囲が広がったことで、探索の労力の違いを確認する前に移動の方向を立証できるから。

choices.text: Older searches near the road may give stronger evidence of high-site absence than later visits give of presence.
choices.text_ja: 道路近くでの古い調査は、後の訪問が生息の証拠となる以上に、高い場所にいないことの強い証拠となるかもしれないから。

choices.text: Higher sites may have contained populations before observers began surveying them.
choices.text_ja: 観察者が調査を始める前から、高い場所に個体群がいた可能性があるから。

choices.text: Fewer high ponds on the older map make each recent high sighting stronger evidence of expansion.
choices.text_ja: 古い地図では高い場所の池が少ないため、最近の高い場所での目撃一つひとつが分布拡大のより強い証拠になるから。

questions.stem: Which comparison would strengthen the investigation of temperature as an influence?
questions.stem_ja: 気温を要因として調べる研究を強化するのは、どのような比較か。

choices.text: Prioritize the highest sites because they have the clearest difference in elevation.
choices.text_ja: 標高の差が最もはっきりしているので、最も高い地点を優先する。

choices.text: Compare the mountain's average warming with the number of new high-altitude dots.
choices.text_ja: 山の平均的な温暖化の程度を、高地での新しい点の数と比較する。

choices.text: Use recent records in place of older ones because they include more sites.
choices.text_ja: より多くの地点を含んでいるので、古い記録の代わりに最近の記録を使う。

choices.text: Examine occupied and abandoned sites with similar important habitat features and recorded local conditions.
choices.text_ja: 生息地の重要な特徴が似ていて、地域の条件が記録されている、カエルのいる場所といなくなった場所を調べる。

questions.stem: Why may temperature and habitat explanations overlap?
questions.stem_ja: なぜ気温による説明と生息地による説明は重なりうるのか。

choices.text: Temperature-related changes can affect the water conditions that support breeding.
choices.text_ja: 気温に関連する変化が、繁殖を支える水の条件に影響しうるから。

choices.text: Sites at the same elevation generally have the same breeding conditions.
choices.text_ja: 同じ標高の地点は、一般に同じ繁殖条件を持っているから。

choices.text: Local drainage changes indicate that the temperature trend is inaccurate.
choices.text_ja: 地域の排水の変化は、気温の傾向が不正確であることを示しているから。

choices.text: A suitable pond makes local temperature less relevant to a population's survival.
choices.text_ja: 適した池があれば、個体群の生存にとって地域の気温はあまり重要でなくなるから。

questions.stem: Why distinguish an individual sighting from evidence of breeding?
questions.stem_ja: なぜ個体の目撃と繁殖の証拠を区別するのか。

choices.text: An animal's presence does not by itself establish a reproducing population at the site.
choices.text_ja: 動物がいるというだけでは、その場所に繁殖する個体群がいることは立証されないから。

choices.text: Individual sightings can be excluded once repeated pond surveys are available.
choices.text_ja: 池の調査が繰り返し行われれば、個体の目撃は除外できるから。

choices.text: A sighting is more sensitive to temperature than a breeding record.
choices.text_ja: 目撃は、繁殖の記録よりも気温の影響を受けやすいから。

choices.text: Breeding records remove the need to account for observation effort.
choices.text_ja: 繁殖の記録があれば、観察の労力を考慮する必要がなくなるから。

questions.stem: Which change in surveys could produce more records without a comparable population increase?
questions.stem_ja: 調査のどのような変化が、それに見合う個体数の増加がないのに記録を増やしうるか。

choices.text: Using the same sites and recording the timing of each search.
choices.text_ja: 同じ地点を使い、それぞれの探索の時期を記録すること。

choices.text: Searching more often during conditions when frogs are easier to detect.
choices.text_ja: カエルを見つけやすい条件のときに、より頻繁に探すこと。

choices.text: Adding pond measurements to the information recorded after each sighting.
choices.text_ja: 目撃のたびに記録する情報に、池の測定値を加えること。

choices.text: Separating confirmed absence from sites that were never visited.
choices.text_ja: いないことが確認された地点と、一度も訪れていない地点とを区別すること。

passage.title: The Price That Appeared Only at Checkout

paragraphs.text: The shopper closed the checkout page just before payment. At the fictional online store Northline, the final total was higher than the price that had first attracted her attention. Delivery and a mandatory handling charge had appeared during the last steps. The store recorded an abandoned purchase, but that record did not explain whether the problem was the total amount, the late disclosure, or a better alternative elsewhere. To understand the decision, it was necessary to go backward through the sequence of comparisons that had brought the shopper to the checkout.

At the beginning, Northline's product page displayed a price below that of another fictional store, Clearcart. The shopper selected Northline and spent time choosing a size and entering details. Clearcart's initial display included standard delivery, whereas Northline's did not. The two numbers therefore referred to different packages of costs. Comparing them as though they described the same transaction gave Northline an apparent advantage before the full price was known. This could matter even if both stores ultimately supplied accurate totals before accepting payment.

The order of information created a second issue beyond the amount itself. Once a shopper has invested effort in selecting an item, restarting elsewhere has a cost in time and attention. Some may continue despite an unexpectedly high total, while others may feel that the earlier comparison was undermined and leave. Late disclosure can therefore affect decisions without requiring every shopper to respond identically. A person who expected delivery charges may react differently from someone who believed the displayed amount was complete. The initial price does not determine a single predictable response.

Northline's managers considered lowering the handling charge after seeing the abandonment figures. Before doing so, they compared two ways of presenting the same final price. In a fictional trial, one page showed the product price with the mandatory charge and standard delivery together near the start. Another retained the existing sequence. The products and total charges were kept comparable, and visitors were assigned to the versions to reduce differences between the groups. This design addressed the timing of disclosure. It did not test whether a lower total price would attract more buyers, because the total itself had not been reduced.

The earlier total reduced abandonment at checkout but also led some visitors to leave sooner. Looking only at the final screen would have exaggerated the improvement. Managers therefore followed the whole sequence from the product page to completed purchase. They also asked customers about the clarity of the price information. A clearer comparison could be valuable even if it allowed some people to decide against buying earlier. The store's desired sales total and the customer's ability to make an informed comparison were related outcomes, not identical ones.

Price was not the only difference between the stores. Clearcart and Northline also had different return arrangements. In the imagined comparison, one offered a longer return period but required the customer to pay return delivery; the other offered a shorter period with return delivery included. Which arrangement was more useful depended partly on the shopper's uncertainty about the item and ability to act within the deadline. Adding the purchase total correctly did not settle this further comparison. Nor could a generous-sounding return period be treated as equivalent to a lower possible cost of returning the item.

The abandoned purchase thus represented the endpoint of several judgments. The shopper had compared incomplete starting prices, encountered a revised total after investing effort, and still needed to consider return conditions. The trial clarified one aspect of that process without explaining every customer's choice. A fair comparison required costs and conditions to be placed on a common basis and made visible when they could inform the decision. Shoppers could then reasonably choose differently because their needs differed. What should not differ unnoticed was the meaning of the numbers they were being invited to compare.

questions.stem: Why did the first displayed prices create an unreliable comparison?
questions.stem_ja: 最初に表示された価格が、信頼できない比較を生んだのはなぜか。

choices.text: Northline's price excluded costs that were included in Clearcart's displayed amount.
choices.text_ja: ノースラインの価格には、クリアカートの表示金額には含まれていた費用が含まれていなかったから。

choices.text: Clearcart included delivery because its customers were more likely to return items.
choices.text_ja: クリアカートの顧客のほうが商品を返品する傾向が強いため、配送料を含めていたから。

choices.text: The stores charged different totals even though the products had different return periods.
choices.text_ja: 商品の返品期間が異なっていたにもかかわらず、ストアごとに異なる合計金額を請求していたから。

choices.text: The shopper had not yet decided which size was suitable at either store.
choices.text_ja: 買い物客が、どちらのストアでもまだどのサイズが合うかを決めていなかったから。

questions.stem: How could the same late charge lead some shoppers to continue and others to leave?
questions.stem_ja: 同じように遅れて表示された料金によって、購入を続ける買い物客と立ち去る買い物客が出てくるのはなぜか。

choices.text: Expecting delivery charges makes the final increase easier to judge, so prior selection effort becomes irrelevant.
choices.text_ja: 配送料を予想していれば最終的な値上がりを判断しやすくなるので、それまでの商品選びの労力は関係なくなるから。

choices.text: Continuing avoids repeating the selection work, so it shows that the revised total is better than alternatives.
choices.text_ja: 購入を続ければ商品選びをやり直さずに済むので、修正された合計金額がほかの選択肢よりよいことを示しているから。

choices.text: Leaving after disclosure shows that the total exceeded a budget, rather than that its presentation mattered.
choices.text_ja: 表示後に立ち去るのは、その示し方が問題だったからではなく、合計金額が予算を超えていたことを示しているから。

choices.text: Their expectations and the cost they place on restarting can differ.
choices.text_ja: 人によって予想していたことや、やり直すことの負担の感じ方が異なりうるから。

questions.stem: What does the fictional trial most directly test?
questions.stem_ja: 架空の試験が最も直接的に検証しているのは何か。

choices.text: Whether Clearcart's price structure better matches Northline's customers.
choices.text_ja: クリアカートの価格体系のほうが、ノースラインの顧客に合っているかどうか。

choices.text: Whether showing a comparable total earlier changes the purchasing process.
choices.text_ja: 同等の合計金額をより早く示すことで、購入の過程が変わるかどうか。

choices.text: Whether reducing handling charges increases the number of purchases.
choices.text_ja: 手数料を下げれば購入件数が増えるかどうか。

choices.text: Whether return delivery costs explain abandonment at the payment screen.
choices.text_ja: 返送料によって、支払い画面での購入中断が説明できるかどうか。

questions.stem: Why assess the whole purchasing sequence rather than checkout abandonment alone?
questions.stem_ja: 支払い画面での購入中断だけでなく、購入の流れ全体を評価するのはなぜか。

choices.text: Earlier departures indicate the total price was displayed incorrectly.
choices.text_ja: 早い段階で立ち去る人がいることは、合計金額が誤って表示されていたことを示しているから。

choices.text: The whole sequence determines whether lowering the total would improve sales.
choices.text_ja: 流れ全体によって、合計金額を下げれば売上が伸びるかどうかが決まるから。

choices.text: Fewer late departures may partly reflect decisions to leave earlier.
choices.text_ja: 最後の段階で立ち去る人が減ったのは、より早い段階で立ち去ることにした人がいたことを一部反映しているかもしれないから。

choices.text: Completed purchases reveal whether customers understood every return condition.
choices.text_ja: 購入が完了したかどうかで、顧客が返品の条件をすべて理解していたかどうかがわかるから。

questions.stem: Why does a longer return period not establish that one store's terms are better for every shopper?
questions.stem_ja: 返品期間が長いからといって、一方のストアの条件がすべての買い物客にとってよいとは言えないのはなぜか。

choices.text: The initial product price determines how long a customer needs to decide.
choices.text_ja: 最初の商品価格によって、顧客が判断するのに必要な期間が決まるから。

choices.text: Included return delivery removes the need to consider a deadline.
choices.text_ja: 返送料が含まれていれば、期限を考慮する必要がなくなるから。

choices.text: Return costs and the shopper's needs also affect the value of the arrangement.
choices.text_ja: 返品にかかる費用や買い物客のニーズも、その条件の価値を左右するから。

choices.text: The longer period is offered only when the customer pays mandatory handling charges.
choices.text_ja: 長い返品期間は、顧客が必ずかかる手数料を支払った場合にのみ提供されるから。

passage.title: A City That Tried to Preserve the Stars

paragraphs.text: At the observatory above fictional Leston, a visitor searched for a constellation she remembered seeing from her childhood street. The brighter stars remained, but the spaces between them looked empty. Down in the town, a nurse finishing a late shift was choosing a route home. She avoided the riverside path because she found its steps difficult to see. Both wanted the council to change its lighting, although a proposal to make the town darker sounded helpful to one and worrying to the other.

The observatory's concern was light traveling beyond the places it was intended to illuminate. Some escaped directly upward; some reached the sky after reflection from surfaces. This unwanted brightness made faint objects harder to distinguish. The astronomers asked the council to examine the direction of its lights as well as their strength. They were not demanding that the nurse walk home without illumination. Nevertheless, a newspaper headline describing their request as a campaign against streetlights made that distinction difficult to explain.

Residents approached the question from the pavement. At a public meeting, several complained about a particularly bright lamp beside the river. Its exposed source was uncomfortable to look toward, yet the steps beneath a nearby tree remained in shadow. Simply increasing the lamp's output had not distributed light where pedestrians needed it. Other residents valued light near the bus stop, especially when waiting alone. The meeting revealed different purposes within a short stretch of street: recognizing a step, seeing an approaching person, and finding a destination were related but distinct needs.

A lighting engineer brought diagrams rather than a single brightness target. Shields could limit light escaping upward or toward nearby windows. Adjusting a fitting could direct illumination onto a path, while several carefully positioned sources might avoid the contrast between a dazzling lamp and a dark obstacle. These choices still required checks. A shield that protected a bedroom could leave a crossing poorly lit if its position was wrong. The engineer therefore asked residents to mark actual walking routes and obstacles before selecting equipment.

The council tried two arrangements. Beside the open square, repositioned fittings lit the walking surfaces while making the sources less visible from the observatory. Near the river, the same fittings left gaps where branches intercepted the light. The team moved some lamps and tested the steps again instead of copying the square's arrangement unchanged. Volunteers walked both routes and reported where they struggled to identify edges. Their observations concerned visibility; the council did not present a short trial as evidence that crime had fallen or that every resident now felt safe.

The observatory noticed an improvement in its view, but could not attribute the entire change to council lamps. Shop windows, private buildings, and conditions in the atmosphere also affected the brightness it observed. It compared repeated observations under similar conditions and asked for records of which public lights had been changed. Meanwhile, the nurse found the revised steps easier to distinguish even though the nearest lamp looked less intense. Her experience illustrated why the appearance of a light source was a poor substitute for examining the surface it was meant to serve.

Leston's final plan separated locations and hours of use. Frequently used routes kept useful illumination, while fittings in empty public areas could operate differently after closing. The observatory gained a reason to support precise lighting rather than compete with every pedestrian demand. Residents gained a way to question both excessive glare and inadequate coverage. Neither group received a guarantee that its concern would disappear. They did, however, replace an argument over whether the town should be bright or dark with decisions about where light traveled, what people needed to see, and how each result would be checked.

questions.stem: Which interpretation best reconciles the astronomers’ request with residents’ concerns?
questions.stem_ja: 天文学者たちの要望と住民たちの懸念を最もよく両立させる解釈はどれか。

choices.text: Reducing light that escapes its intended area can be compatible with improving visibility along particular routes.
choices.text_ja: 照らすべき範囲から漏れる光を減らすことは、特定の道での見えやすさを改善することと両立しうる。

choices.text: Lowering the town’s overall output would address both concerns before the locations of individual lights mattered.
choices.text_ja: 町全体の光量を下げれば、個々の照明の位置を問題にする前に、両方の懸念に対処できる。

choices.text: Improving visibility near the river would require accepting the same amount of unwanted light above the town.
choices.text_ja: 川沿いの見えやすさを改善するには、町の上空に同じ量の不要な光が出ることを受け入れなければならない。

choices.text: Maintaining the brightest sources near public routes would meet residents’ needs while shielding elsewhere helped observers.
choices.text_ja: 公共の道の近くでは最も明るい光源を維持し、それ以外の場所で遮光すれば、住民の必要を満たしつつ観測者の役にも立つ。

questions.stem: Why did the engineer ask residents to mark obstacles before choosing equipment?
questions.stem_ja: 技師が、機器を選ぶ前に住民に障害物を書き込むよう頼んだのはなぜか。

choices.text: The resulting map would establish a common output level suitable for the whole riverside.
choices.text_ja: できあがった地図によって、川沿い全体に適した共通の光量を定められるから。

choices.text: The useful distribution of light depended on the tasks and surfaces within each route.
choices.text_ja: どのように光を配分すれば役に立つかは、各ルートにおける目的や地面によって決まるから。

choices.text: The marked routes would identify which residents were most affected by light entering their bedrooms.
choices.text_ja: 書き込まれたルートから、寝室に入る光の影響を最も受けている住民が分かるから。

choices.text: Residents’ preferred routes would show where exposed light sources could replace shielded fittings.
choices.text_ja: 住民が好むルートから、むき出しの光源を遮光された器具の代わりに使える場所が分かるから。

questions.stem: What does the contrast between the square and riverside trials imply for another wooded path?
questions.stem_ja: 広場での試験と川沿いでの試験の違いは、別の木の多い小道について何を示唆しているか。

choices.text: The observers’ view should determine placement because their measurements can include both paths together.
choices.text_ja: 観測者の測定は両方の道を一緒に含められるので、観測者の見え方によって配置を決めるべきである。

choices.text: The fitting design could be retained for testing, but its placement would need checking against local obstructions.
choices.text_ja: 器具の設計は試験のためにそのまま使えるかもしれないが、その配置は地元の障害物に照らして確かめる必要がある。

choices.text: A more intense source should be selected before route testing because the river trial exposed insufficient output.
choices.text_ja: 川沿いの試験で光量の不足が明らかになったので、ルートの試験の前により強い光源を選ぶべきである。

choices.text: The square’s spacing would provide the strongest starting evidence because its arrangement had already succeeded.
choices.text_ja: 広場の配置はすでに成功しているので、その間隔が最も有力な出発点となる。

questions.stem: Which claim exceeds the evidence reported from the trial?
questions.stem_ja: 試験から報告された証拠の範囲を超えている主張はどれか。

choices.text: The nurse’s experience distinguished the appearance of a lamp from visibility of the walking surface.
choices.text_ja: 看護師の経験は、街灯の見た目と歩く地面の見えやすさとを区別するものだった。

choices.text: Changes outside the public lighting system complicated interpretation of the observatory’s observations.
choices.text_ja: 公共の照明以外の変化が、天文台の観測結果の解釈を難しくした。

choices.text: The redesigned route lowered the local crime rate because volunteers could identify its steps more easily.
choices.text_ja: ボランティアが階段をより見分けやすくなったので、改修されたルートによって地域の犯罪率が下がった。

choices.text: The usefulness of the fittings varied with nearby features despite an unchanged equipment design.
choices.text_ja: 器具の設計は変わらなかったにもかかわらず、その有用性は周囲の地形や物によって異なった。

questions.stem: Why would records of changed public lamps help the observatory’s assessment?
questions.stem_ja: 変更された公共の街灯の記録が、天文台の評価に役立つのはなぜか。

choices.text: They would make volunteers’ judgments of route visibility comparable to measurements of faint stars.
choices.text_ja: ボランティアによる道の見えやすさの判断を、かすかな星の測定と比較できるようになるから。

choices.text: They would identify the hours when private buildings should use the same settings as public areas.
choices.text_ja: 私有の建物が公共の場所と同じ設定を使うべき時間帯が分かるから。

choices.text: They would allow clear observations to be treated as the result of council action rather than atmospheric conditions.
choices.text_ja: 星がよく見えた観測を、大気の状態ではなく町議会の対策の結果として扱えるようになるから。

choices.text: They would connect particular interventions with observations while leaving other influences to be considered.
choices.text_ja: ほかの影響も考慮すべきものとして残しつつ、特定の対策を観測結果と結びつけられるから。

passage.title: The Footpath That Became a Legal Question

paragraphs.text: The school bus was visible through the bars, but the gate between it and the children was locked. In the fictional village of Harrowmere, families had crossed this strip of farmland for years to reach the main road. The new owner regarded it as a route through a working property, not a public facility. Parents regarded the closure as the removal of an ordinary part of village life. Their disagreement began with a practical interruption, but quickly produced two different questions: who owned the land, and who was entitled to cross it?

The owner brought a recent boundary plan to the village meeting. The disputed path lay inside his property, and he wanted to keep walkers away from vehicles entering a storage yard. He also pointed to the cost of repairing a damaged fence. To him, the plan confirmed responsibility as well as control. Residents did not challenge the boundary line. They argued instead that a route could cross someone's land while carrying an established right of passage. Proving ownership would therefore answer one question without necessarily resolving the other.

The residents assembled photographs, old maps, and recollections of daily journeys. A map showed a narrow line following much of the present route. However, its key did not distinguish a public path from a private track. Photographs established that people had walked there, but rarely showed whether they had permission. One former resident remembered the old owner welcoming schoolchildren; another remembered walkers passing without asking. These accounts supported a long history of use more clearly than they supported a single explanation of the conditions under which that use occurred.

A legal adviser refused to turn that history into an immediate verdict. Rules governing access differ between legal systems, and the relevance of repeated use can depend on circumstances such as permission, continuity, and the kind of route involved. She was not applying a universal rule that a certain number of journeys creates a right. In Harrowmere's case, records of agreements and any formal recognition of the route needed investigation. She asked the village to preserve its evidence, while warning both sides that a familiar practice and a legally enforceable entitlement were not interchangeable.

The council meanwhile measured an alternative route. On a map it added little distance, but it followed a road without a continuous footway and required crossing near a bend. The shortest line was not necessarily the easiest journey for children. The owner suggested another path around the edge of his field, away from the storage yard. That route avoided moving vehicles on his property, but passed over ground that became difficult after rain. These comparisons did not establish anyone's legal rights. They showed what different arrangements would mean in everyday use.

Negotiations could therefore proceed alongside the investigation, provided that their purpose remained clear. A temporary agreement opened the existing path during school travel times, with a marked boundary separating walkers from the yard. The parties recorded that this arrangement did not settle the disputed legal position. It reduced the immediate inconvenience while leaving room to inspect the field-edge route and search for earlier agreements. Some residents disliked the restricted hours; the owner remained concerned about maintenance. Their cooperation was useful precisely because it did not require either side to pretend that every question had been answered.

The closed gate had made an invisible dependency visible: daily travel relied on an arrangement that people had rarely needed to describe. Harrowmere could assess the burdens of alternative routes without assuming that convenience created a right, and investigate rights without assuming that ownership settled access. The practical and legal questions informed each other but required different evidence. Whatever permanent arrangement emerged, recording its route, conditions, and responsibilities would help future residents and owners understand what the present generation had once left unstated.

questions.stem: Why does the boundary plan fail to resolve the residents’ argument by itself?
questions.stem_ja: 境界図だけでは住民の主張に決着がつかないのはなぜか。

choices.text: The plan concerns the new owner’s responsibilities, whereas the residents dispute his responsibility for repairs.
choices.text_ja: 図面は新しい所有者の責任に関するものだが、住民は修理に対する彼の責任に異議を唱えているから。

choices.text: The residents regard repeated journeys as evidence that the mapped boundary has gradually moved.
choices.text_ja: 住民は、繰り返し行き来してきたことを、図面上の境界が徐々に移動してきた証拠とみなしているから。

choices.text: The residents question crossing rights within the property rather than the location of its ownership boundary.
choices.text_ja: 住民が問題にしているのは、所有地の境界の位置ではなく、敷地内を通行する権利だから。

choices.text: The photographs provide a more recent account of ownership than the plan brought to the meeting.
choices.text_ja: 写真の方が、集会に持ち込まれた図面よりも新しい所有関係を示しているから。

questions.stem: Which additional finding would address a key uncertainty in the residents’ evidence?
questions.stem_ja: 住民の証拠における重要な不確かさを解消するのは、どのような追加の発見か。

choices.text: A clearer boundary plan showing the full extent of the new owner’s farmland.
choices.text_ja: 新しい所有者の農地の範囲全体を示す、より明確な境界図。

choices.text: An account demonstrating that the route was more convenient than the main-road alternative.
choices.text_ja: そのルートが幹線道路沿いの代替ルートよりも便利だったことを示す証言。

choices.text: More photographs showing how many people used the path on busy school mornings.
choices.text_ja: 通学で混み合う朝に、何人がその小道を利用していたかを示す追加の写真。

choices.text: A surviving agreement explaining whether earlier crossings were permitted and under what conditions.
choices.text_ja: 以前の通行が許可されていたかどうか、またどのような条件のもとでだったかを説明する、現存する取り決め。

questions.stem: What is the significance of the temporary agreement’s recorded limitation?
questions.stem_ja: 暫定的な合意に限定事項が記録されたことには、どのような意味があるか。

choices.text: It allows immediate cooperation without treating that cooperation as a final determination of the disputed right.
choices.text_ja: 争われている権利についての最終的な判断とはみなさずに、すぐに協力することができる。

choices.text: It allows the owner to treat the restricted hours as evidence that the earlier route was private.
choices.text_ja: 所有者は、時間の制限を、以前のルートが私道だった証拠として扱うことができる。

choices.text: It gives the residents a new historical record that confirms their interpretation of earlier use.
choices.text_ja: 住民は、以前の利用についての自分たちの解釈を裏づける新たな歴史的記録を得る。

choices.text: It replaces the search for old agreements with a more practical test of school travel needs.
choices.text_ja: 古い取り決めの調査を、通学の必要性についてのより実際的な検証に置き換える。

questions.stem: Which assessment best follows the passage when comparing the alternative routes?
questions.stem_ja: 別のルートを比較する際の評価として、本文の内容に最も沿っているのはどれか。

choices.text: The dangers of the road provide stronger proof of an existing right than uncertain records of earlier permission.
choices.text_ja: 道路の危険性は、以前の許可についての不確かな記録よりも、既存の権利の強い証拠となる。

choices.text: Their walking conditions matter to a workable arrangement, even though those conditions do not establish access rights.
choices.text_ja: 歩く際の条件は、通行の権利を確定するものではないが、実行可能な取り決めにとっては重要である。

choices.text: The road’s shorter measured length gives it priority unless the residents establish ownership of the field route.
choices.text_ja: 住民が畑のルートの所有権を立証しない限り、測定上の距離が短い道路が優先される。

choices.text: The field-edge route resolves the owner’s concerns because avoiding yard traffic also removes maintenance questions.
choices.text_ja: 置き場を出入りする車両を避ければ保守の問題もなくなるので、畑の縁のルートで所有者の懸念は解消される。

questions.stem: Why had the status of the route remained difficult to describe until the closure?
questions.stem_ja: 閉鎖されるまで、その道の位置づけを説明するのが難しいままだったのはなぜか。

choices.text: Routine use had continued without forcing people to distinguish its practical role from the terms supporting access.
choices.text_ja: 日常的な利用が続いていたため、人々はその道の実際上の役割と、通行を支える条件とを区別する必要に迫られなかったから。

choices.text: The history of repeated journeys had been treated as sufficient evidence without separating permission from an established entitlement.
choices.text_ja: 繰り返し行き来してきた歴史が、許可と確立した権利とを区別しないまま、十分な証拠として扱われていたから。

choices.text: Residents had understood the conditions of access but disagreed about which alternative route to choose.
choices.text_ja: 住民は通行の条件を理解していたが、どの代替ルートを選ぶかについて意見が分かれていたから。

choices.text: The old map had made people confident about public access even though its key described the route without classifying that access.
choices.text_ja: 古い地図の凡例はルートを示すだけで通行の種類を分類していなかったのに、その地図のせいで人々が公共の通行に確信を持っていたから。

passage.title: The Crystal That Produced a Tiny Current

paragraphs.text: The needle moves when a small crystal is pressed, then settles as the demonstrator holds the pressure steady. When the pressure is released, it briefly moves in the opposite direction. Imagine watching this classroom demonstration without knowing what is inside the apparatus. The movements suggest a connection between force and electricity, but they leave several explanations open. Perhaps the leads have moved, perhaps the instrument is responding to an unnoticed disturbance, or perhaps the crystal itself produces an electrical change when its shape changes.

The demonstrator begins by securing the connecting wires and repeating the action without touching them. The response still follows the pressing and releasing. She then replaces the crystal with an ordinary block in the same holder. Under the same procedure, the earlier response does not appear. This comparison makes movement of the holder a less convincing explanation, although one comparison cannot identify every possible source of error. Repeating the sequence and recording the conditions is more informative than displaying the largest movement once and calling it a discovery.

Certain materials have an internal arrangement of electrical charges that can become unbalanced when the material is deformed. Pressing such a crystal changes the arrangement slightly, creating a difference in electrical potential between suitable surfaces. With an appropriate connection, charge can move through a circuit. This is the piezoelectric effect. The crystal is converting some of the mechanical input into an electrical response, rather than supplying energy independently of the person pressing it. The word 'electricity' describes a result, but does not tell us how much useful energy the arrangement can deliver.

The return of the needle introduces another distinction. In this demonstration, the measuring circuit allows charge to leak away over time. A reading that fades while the force remains steady therefore does not necessarily mean that the force has disappeared. Changes in force are easier for this arrangement to reveal than an indefinitely maintained load. The demonstrator compares repeated presses using the same circuit and mounting. She does not conclude that any brief signal from any crystal would provide an accurate measurement of weight. The electrical circuit is part of the measuring system, not a transparent window onto the material.

Next she compares gentle and stronger changes in pressure. Within the range she tests, the stronger changes produce larger responses. Before using those responses to estimate force, she would need known inputs and repeated measurements to establish a dependable relationship. Changing the crystal's mounting or the circuit could change that relationship. The classroom observations support investigating a sensor, but they do not yet supply a ready-made scale. Even a repeatable signal needs interpretation: it might indicate the timing of an event more reliably than its exact size.

Consider a machine that makes a small vibration during each normal cycle. A suitable sensor could convert those changing forces into an electrical record. A departure from the usual pattern would give engineers a reason to inspect the machine, even if the signal contained too little energy to operate the machine itself. It would not identify the cause of the departure without further evidence. A loose attachment, a changed operating condition, and damage to a moving part could produce different explanations for a changed record. The value lies first in noticing and describing the event.

The classroom experiment thus develops from a moving needle into two separate questions. Can a controlled mechanical input produce a repeatable electrical response? Can that response provide useful information in a particular application? Generating substantial power would require a different assessment of available mechanical energy, losses, and demand. A tiny signal may be disappointing as a power supply while being valuable as a measurement. Understanding that difference gives the modest demonstration a practical meaning without turning it into a promise of effortless energy.

questions.stem: What does replacing the crystal with an ordinary block contribute to the demonstration?
questions.stem_ja: 結晶をふつうのブロックに取り替えることは、実演にどのような貢献をしているか。

choices.text: It tests whether the earlier response can be explained by pressing the holder without the original material.
choices.text_ja: 元の物質がない状態でホルダーを押すことによって、さきほどの反応が説明できるかどうかを検証している。

choices.text: It separates the effect of pressing the crystal from the effect of changing the measuring circuit.
choices.text_ja: 結晶を押すことの効果を、測定回路を変えることの効果と切り分けている。

choices.text: It establishes the range of forces for which the original crystal can provide an accurate measurement.
choices.text_ja: 元の結晶が正確な測定を行える力の範囲を確定している。

choices.text: It determines whether charge disappears faster from the original crystal than from the replacement.
choices.text_ja: 電荷が、取り替えたブロックよりも元の結晶から速く失われるかどうかを判定している。

questions.stem: Why could a small electrical response still have practical value?
questions.stem_ja: 小さな電気的反応でも、なお実用的な価値をもちうるのはなぜか。

choices.text: Its limited energy could make it less sensitive to changes in the mounting or operating conditions.
choices.text_ja: エネルギーが小さいため、取り付け方や運転条件の変化の影響を受けにくくなりうるから。

choices.text: Its repeated appearance could identify the damaged component without comparisons with normal operation.
choices.text_ja: 繰り返し現れることで、通常の運転と比較しなくても損傷した部品を特定できるから。

choices.text: Its usefulness as a record could establish that larger crystals would provide enough energy to drive the machine.
choices.text_ja: 記録として役立つことから、より大きな結晶なら機械を動かすのに十分なエネルギーを供給できると立証できるから。

choices.text: It could record a change worth investigating even when it supplies little of the energy an application needs.
choices.text_ja: 用途に必要なエネルギーをほとんど供給できなくても、調べる価値のある変化を記録できるから。

questions.stem: Why would treating the fading reading as evidence of a disappearing force be mistaken here?
questions.stem_ja: ここで、測定値が小さくなっていくことを力が消えていく証拠とみなすのが誤りなのはなぜか。

choices.text: The controlled comparison had already linked a maintained load to a permanent reading.
choices.text_ja: 管理された比較によって、かかり続ける荷重が一定の測定値と結びつけられていたから。

choices.text: The release signal allows the earlier steady load to be reconstructed without considering the circuit.
choices.text_ja: 緩めたときの信号から、回路を考慮しなくても、それ以前の一定の荷重を再構成できるから。

choices.text: The circuit can lose charge while the mechanical load remains in place.
choices.text_ja: 機械的な荷重がかかったままでも、回路から電荷が失われることがあるから。

choices.text: Larger responses to stronger presses establish the remaining force throughout each hold.
choices.text_ja: 強く押したときの反応が大きいことから、押し続けているあいだ残っている力がわかるから。

questions.stem: After changing the mounting, what would be most appropriate before interpreting signal size as force?
questions.stem_ja: 取り付け方を変えたあと、信号の大きさを力として解釈する前に行うべきことして最も適切なものはどれか。

choices.text: Retain the old relationship if the signal still appears whenever the crystal is pressed.
choices.text_ja: 結晶を押すたびに信号がまだ現れるなら、以前の関係をそのまま使う。

choices.text: Compare responses to known inputs again using the revised arrangement.
choices.text_ja: 変更後の装置で、既知の入力に対する反応をもう一度比較する。

choices.text: Extend the duration of each press until the reading represents the maintained load.
choices.text_ja: 測定値がかかり続ける荷重を表すようになるまで、一回ごとに押す時間を延ばす。

choices.text: Use the largest previous response as the new limit for interpreting smaller signals.
choices.text_ja: 以前に得られた最大の反応を、より小さな信号を解釈するための新たな上限とする。

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the sequence of tests?
questions.stem_ja: 一連の検証によって最もよく裏づけられる結論はどれか。

choices.text: Known inputs make mounting differences unimportant, while repeatable anomalies identify a damaged component.
choices.text_ja: 既知の入力があれば取り付け方の違いは重要でなくなり、繰り返し現れる異常によって損傷した部品が特定できる。

choices.text: Normal-cycle comparisons distinguish equipment faults from operating changes, although power output remains uncertain.
choices.text_ja: 通常の周期との比較によって装置の故障と運転条件の変化とを見分けられるが、電力の出力は不確かなままである。

choices.text: Repeatability supports further measurement development, while calibration and causal interpretation remain additional tasks.
choices.text_ja: 再現性があることは測定方法をさらに開発することを支持するが、較正と原因の解釈は別の課題として残る。

choices.text: Repeated responses establish a transferable calibration, though unexpected machine signals still require investigation.
choices.text_ja: 繰り返し得られる反応によって、ほかの装置にも通用する較正が確立されるが、機械からの予期しない信号はなお調査が必要である。

passage.title: The Forest Survey Made from Footprints

paragraphs.text: A photograph in the fictional Fenmere Forest survey shows a line of footprints beside a measuring stick. Red marks indicate the prints that volunteers counted. On a neighboring page, a rocky trail has no marks at all. At first glance, the contrast seems to show where the forest's rare wildcat is most numerous. The survey leader asks the group to pause. The photographs record traces that were visible during a visit. Between the animal's movement and the red marks lie several processes that may change what the survey appears to say.

Volunteers walk fixed routes, photograph suspected wildcat prints, and record the surface and recent weather. A specialist checks the photographs because similar animals can leave confusing traces. Even after identification, a set of prints establishes passage more directly than population size. An animal may leave many prints during one crossing, and the same animal may use a route again. Conversely, another animal can cross without leaving a trace the volunteers recognize. Counting carefully improves the record of visible evidence; it does not automatically turn that record into a count of individuals.

The muddy route illustrates both advantages and difficulties. Soft ground records details that hard rock does not retain, but heavy rain can erase marks before the next visit. Light rain may instead prepare a fresh surface on which later movement becomes easy to detect. The meaning of a wet morning therefore depends on when the rain fell relative to the animals' passage and the survey. Recording 'rainy' beside a total is less informative than noting the timing and condition of the ground. A low count after a storm may describe lost evidence rather than reduced activity.

A narrow crossing adds a different problem. Volunteers find tracks there repeatedly because it connects two sheltered parts of the forest. Several animals could be using it, but one animal making repeated journeys could also contribute many records. Simply expanding the survey along the same crossing would provide more observations of that route, not necessarily a broader picture of the forest. To investigate distribution, the team also needs routes with different positions and surface conditions. Their choice of where to look is part of the result they obtain.

The team installs automatic cameras near selected routes to compare images with the tracks. At the crossing, photographs reveal repeated visits by an animal with a recognizable mark on its flank. This confirms one source of repeated records; it does not prove that every track there belongs to that animal. At the rocky route, a camera records a wildcat even though volunteers find no usable prints. That observation directly challenges the interpretation that an empty footprint record means absence. Cameras have limits too: a passing animal may remain outside the frame, and photographs may lack features that distinguish individuals.

For the next round, volunteers repeat routes on a consistent schedule and record recent weather more precisely. They keep camera records and footprint records separate before comparing them, rather than adding both totals as if each represented a different animal. A track and an image may record the same visit. The team also reports how much of each surface was examined, so readers can distinguish a long searched area from a short one. Standardizing effort reduces one source of confusion while leaving differences in detection to be considered.

Fenmere's final map marks confirmed evidence of use and locations where searches produced no evidence. It does not label the latter as places without wildcats. The concentrated tracks at the crossing justify closer study of an important route, not a precise claim about how many animals live nearby. By combining methods without confusing their units, the survey can guide future observation and habitat decisions. Its restraint is informative: it identifies what has been seen, what may explain the pattern, and where another kind of evidence could change the interpretation.

questions.stem: Why is the muddy-route total insufficient to show that more wildcats live there than near the rocky route?
questions.stem_ja: ぬかるんだルートの合計数だけでは、岩だらけのルートの近くよりもそこに多くのヤマネコがすんでいると示すのに不十分なのはなぜか。

choices.text: The surfaces differ in retaining visible traces, and multiple traces need not represent different animals.
choices.text_ja: 地面によって目に見える痕跡の残りやすさが異なり、また、複数の痕跡が必ずしも異なる動物を表すとは限らないから。

choices.text: The red marks distinguish separate crossings, but do not show whether those crossings happened before rain.
choices.text_ja: 赤い印は別々の通過を区別しているが、それらの通過が雨の前に起きたかどうかは示していないから。

choices.text: The photographs describe movement accurately enough that the remaining uncertainty concerns where the animals sleep.
choices.text_ja: 写真は移動を十分正確に記録しているので、残る不確かさは動物がどこで眠るかに関するものだけだから。

choices.text: The specialist’s identification makes totals comparable only when the two routes have equal camera coverage.
choices.text_ja: 専門家による識別で合計数が比較可能になるのは、二つのルートのカメラによる撮影範囲が等しい場合だけだから。

questions.stem: Why does the team record the timing of rain rather than just whether a day was wet?
questions.stem_ja: チームが、雨の日だったかどうかだけでなく、雨が降った時期を記録するのはなぜか。

choices.text: A wet surface makes search duration less relevant, so timing can replace records of survey effort.
choices.text_ja: 地面が濡れていると捜索時間はあまり関係なくなるので、時期の記録が調査の労力の記録の代わりになるから。

choices.text: Rain timing allows volunteers to identify the animal responsible for repeated visits to a crossing.
choices.text_ja: 雨の時期が分かれば、通り道を繰り返し訪れている動物をボランティアが特定できるから。

choices.text: Rain can prepare a recording surface or erase existing traces, depending on its relation to passage and observation.
choices.text_ja: 雨は、動物の通過や観察との時間的な関係によって、跡が残る地面を整えることもあれば、すでにある痕跡を消すこともあるから。

choices.text: The time of rain establishes whether wildcats changed their preferred routes during the survey.
choices.text_ja: 雨の時期によって、調査期間中にヤマネコが好むルートを変えたかどうかが確定できるから。

questions.stem: What does the marked animal in the crossing photographs establish?
questions.stem_ja: 通り道の写真に写った模様のある動物から、何が確かめられるか。

choices.text: Repeated visits by one animal contribute to the records, while other animals may also use the crossing.
choices.text_ja: 一頭の動物が繰り返し訪れることが記録の一因になっているが、ほかの動物もその通り道を使っている可能性がある。

choices.text: Additional visits to the crossing will reveal forest-wide distribution more efficiently than searches elsewhere.
choices.text_ja: 通り道への訪問をさらに増やせば、ほかの場所を探すよりも効率よく森全体の分布が明らかになる。

choices.text: The crossing supports fewer animals than other routes because one visitor can be identified repeatedly.
choices.text_ja: 一頭が繰り返し識別できるので、その通り道を利用している動物はほかのルートより少ない。

choices.text: The visible tracks can be assigned to that individual whenever its image appears during the survey period.
choices.text_ja: 調査期間中にその個体の画像が写っていれば、目に見える足跡はその個体のものとみなせる。

questions.stem: Why should the team avoid adding the number of images to the number of track records?
questions.stem_ja: チームが画像の数を足跡の記録の数に足し合わせるべきでないのはなぜか。

choices.text: Camera totals already account for search effort, whereas track totals first need adjustment for weather.
choices.text_ja: カメラの合計数はすでに捜索の労力を考慮しているが、足跡の合計数はまず天候に合わせて補正する必要があるから。

choices.text: The methods sample different surfaces, so combining totals would necessarily give rocky routes more influence.
choices.text_ja: 二つの方法は異なる地面を対象としているので、合計を合わせると必然的に岩だらけのルートの影響が大きくなるから。

choices.text: Images describe individuals and footprints describe routes, so their totals represent separate populations.
choices.text_ja: 画像は個体を表し、足跡はルートを表すので、それぞれの合計は別々の個体群を表しているから。

choices.text: Both methods may describe a single visit, so their sum could count evidence from that visit twice.
choices.text_ja: 両方の方法が一回の同じ訪問を記録している可能性があり、合計するとその訪問の証拠を二重に数えかねないから。

questions.stem: How should the camera observation on the rocky route affect the final map?
questions.stem_ja: 岩だらけのルートでのカメラによる観察は、最終的な地図にどう反映されるべきか。

choices.text: It makes the rocky route a better-supported location of high population density than the crossing.
choices.text_ja: 岩だらけのルートを、通り道よりも個体密度の高い場所としてより強く裏づける。

choices.text: It supports evidence of use there despite the lack of identifiable footprints.
choices.text_ja: 識別できる足跡がなくても、そこが利用されている証拠を裏づける。

choices.text: It shows that future empty camera records there can be treated as evidence of absence.
choices.text_ja: 今後そこでカメラに何も写らなければ、いないことの証拠として扱えることを示す。

choices.text: It allows other trackless rocky areas to be marked as confirmed wildcat habitat.
choices.text_ja: 足跡のないほかの岩場も、ヤマネコの生息地として確認済みと表示できるようにする。

passage.title: The Local Festival That Reached a Global Audience

paragraphs.text: Messages arrived from places the performers had never visited. Viewers praised the drums, asked about the embroidered coats, and shared clips with friends. In fictional Renswick, a volunteer had posted part of the annual harbor festival online. By the next rehearsal, the film had reached an audience far larger than the town square could hold. A sponsor called this proof that the tradition had secured its future. The musicians were pleased, but the oldest drummer asked who would help mend the instruments before the next season.

At rehearsals, the festival existed as a collection of learned tasks. Young players followed older ones through changes in rhythm, while another group repaired costumes and prepared the processional route. Knowing a melody was not enough to coordinate the performance: musicians listened for signals from dancers and adjusted when the procession slowed. These exchanges were difficult to capture in a short film. The volunteer had selected a striking section because it worked well on a small screen, not because it represented every skill needed to hold the event.

Online, that selection acquired a life of its own. Viewers replayed the dramatic ending and asked for more performances like it. The sponsor proposed a separate filmed stage show, with shorter introductions and a faster final section. Some musicians welcomed a chance to earn money and reach new listeners. Others worried that preparing the show would compete with the rehearsals where beginners learned the longer sequence. Both reactions concerned the same opportunity: publicity could bring resources, but using those resources and demands required decisions within the town.

The next planning meeting made the distinction concrete. Extra donations paid for materials to repair costumes, yet the people able to do the repairs were already busy preparing the stage show. More money had eased one constraint without removing another. Meanwhile, several teenagers joined after seeing the clip. They knew the famous ending but needed practice with the quieter passages linking it to the rest of the procession. Their enthusiasm was genuine. Whether it became lasting participation depended partly on the availability of teachers and occasions to practice.

An overseas music group then sent a recording of its own version. Its members had learned the visible rhythm accurately, but replaced the procession with a seated performance and gave the piece a different ending. Renswick's players disagreed over the result. One heard an inventive response; another felt that the piece's local purpose had become invisible. The recording showed that the music was being used beyond its original setting. It did not establish either that Renswick's festival had disappeared or that the overseas group was continuing all of its practices.

The volunteer returned to the rehearsal room with a different filming plan. Alongside short performances, she recorded conversations about learning signals, repairing objects, and organizing the route. The musicians kept the stage show, but limited the preparation time it could take from beginner sessions. They also used some donations to pay experienced members for teaching. These choices did not make every online viewer a participant. They connected part of the new attention to activities that the local event required, rather than assuming that attention would perform that work by itself.

When the next festival approached, the committee examined more than viewing figures. It asked whether beginners returned, whether repairs were completed, and whether enough people could lead the procession. Those questions did not diminish the pleasure of an international audience. They distinguished visible popularity from the capacity to perform again. Renswick's music could travel, change, and attract newcomers while remaining rooted in work carried out locally. The future of the festival depended less on preserving a single image of authenticity than on keeping the relationships through which its practices could be learned and renewed.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between the sponsor’s early judgment and the committee’s later assessment?
questions.stem_ja: スポンサーの当初の判断と委員会の後の評価との主な違いは何か。

choices.text: The sponsor counted viewers directly, whereas the committee used returning beginners to predict future online audience growth.
choices.text_ja: スポンサーは視聴者数を直接数えたが、委員会は戻ってきた初心者の数を使って今後のオンライン視聴者の増加を予測した。

choices.text: The sponsor emphasized new resources, whereas the committee postponed teaching until donations had met every repair need.
choices.text_ja: スポンサーは新たな資源を重視したが、委員会は寄付で修理の必要がすべて満たされるまで指導を延期した。

choices.text: The sponsor valued overseas viewers, whereas the committee considered overseas performances evidence of cultural loss.
choices.text_ja: スポンサーは海外の視聴者を重視したが、委員会は海外での演奏を文化が失われた証拠とみなした。

choices.text: The sponsor treated audience reach as security, whereas the committee examined the capacity to repeat the festival.
choices.text_ja: スポンサーは観客への広がりを安泰の証とみなしたが、委員会は祭りを再び行う力を検討した。

questions.stem: Why did additional donations fail to settle the costume-repair problem immediately?
questions.stem_ja: 追加の寄付によって、衣装修理の問題がすぐに解決しなかったのはなぜか。

choices.text: They provided materials while the preparation of another performance occupied people with the necessary skills.
choices.text_ja: 寄付で材料は手に入ったが、必要な技能を持つ人々が別の公演の準備にかかりきりだったから。

choices.text: They funded practical work, but preparing the shorter performance reduced the number of costumes needed for the procession.
choices.text_ja: 寄付で実際の作業の費用はまかなえたが、短い公演の準備によって行列に必要な衣装の数が減ったから。

choices.text: They supplied materials, but the quieter musical passages had to be mastered before costume repair could begin.
choices.text_ja: 寄付で材料は手に入ったが、衣装の修理を始める前に静かな演奏箇所を習得しなければならなかったから。

choices.text: They supported repairs, but commitments to pay teachers had already used the time available for the stage show.
choices.text_ja: 寄付は修理を支えたが、指導者に謝礼を払う約束のために、舞台公演に使える時間がすでに使われていたから。

questions.stem: What best explains the decision to protect beginner sessions?
questions.stem_ja: 初心者向けの練習時間を守るという決定を最もよく説明するものはどれか。

choices.text: Familiarity with the ending allowed teachers to focus on attracting more viewers rather than rehearsing the longer sequence.
choices.text_ja: 結末の部分になじみがあるので、指導者は長い一連の流れを練習するよりも視聴者を増やすことに集中できたから。

choices.text: The additional explanatory films could replace some rehearsals once beginners recognized the signals on screen.
choices.text_ja: 初心者が画面上で合図を見分けられるようになれば、追加の解説映像で一部のリハーサルを代用できたから。

choices.text: Learning to participate required sustained instruction that enthusiasm for a memorable clip did not provide.
choices.text_ja: 参加できるようになるには継続的な指導が必要であり、印象的な動画への熱意だけではそれが得られなかったから。

choices.text: Older players could transfer their coordination skills most effectively by filming the ending again.
choices.text_ja: 年長の奏者は、結末を撮影し直すことで、最も効果的に息を合わせる技能を伝えられたから。

questions.stem: Which conclusion about the overseas recording is justified?
questions.stem_ja: 海外からの録音について、正当化される結論はどれか。

choices.text: It demonstrated that adaptation abroad was already replacing the quieter passages in Renswick’s own festival.
choices.text_ja: 海外での改変が、すでにレンズウィック自身の祭りの静かな箇所に取って代わりつつあることを示した。

choices.text: It demonstrated musical adaptation abroad without showing that the full local practice was being continued there.
choices.text_ja: 海外で音楽が改変されたことを示したが、地元の慣習の全体がそこで受け継がれていることは示さなかった。

choices.text: It demonstrated that the players agreed that international attention weakened their own performance tradition.
choices.text_ja: 国際的な注目が自分たちの演奏の伝統を弱めたという点で、演奏者たちの意見が一致していることを示した。

choices.text: It demonstrated that accurate rhythm was sufficient to preserve the social purpose of the local procession.
choices.text_ja: 正確なリズムさえあれば、地元の行列が持つ社会的な目的を保つのに十分であることを示した。

questions.stem: Which observation would most directly support the committee’s aim for the new teaching payments?
questions.stem_ja: 新たな指導の謝礼に込めた委員会のねらいを、最も直接的に裏づける観察はどれか。

choices.text: The filmed ending receives more favorable responses after the teachers appear in a new clip.
choices.text_ja: 指導者が新しい動画に登場した後、撮影された結末の部分がより好意的な反応を得る。

choices.text: More overseas groups produce versions with the same rhythm and different settings.
choices.text_ja: 同じリズムで場の設定が異なる版を作る海外のグループが増える。

choices.text: Returning beginners learn the signals well enough to take roles in the next procession.
choices.text_ja: 戻ってきた初心者が、次の行列で役割を担えるほど合図をしっかり身につける。

choices.text: Donations cover all costume materials before the repair group has scheduled its work.
choices.text_ja: 修理グループが作業の予定を立てる前に、寄付で衣装の材料がすべてまかなわれる。

passage.title: The Vaccine Fridge with Two Thermometers

paragraphs.text: Two displays showed different temperatures beside the same refrigerator. At a fictional community clinic in Avenby, the morning worker wondered whether a thermometer needed replacing. One reading came from a probe near the door; the other came from a probe farther inside. Both had seemed dependable during earlier checks. The refrigerator held vaccines, so the staff took the discrepancy seriously. They followed the clinic's procedures for checking stored products while investigating the measurements. They did not decide that the supplies were usable, or unusable, by choosing the more reassuring display.

The technician first asked what each reading represented. Were the displays showing current temperatures, or values recorded at different times? Were the probes measuring the same kind of environment? A probe exposed to air can react differently from one surrounded by material that slows its response. For this investigation, the two probes were the same type, but their clocks and positions still required checking. The word 'temperature' was not enough to make the numbers directly comparable. A measurement included a place, a time, and a method of responding to change.

An instrument fault was one possible explanation. To examine it, the technician placed both probes together in a controlled comparison outside the storage unit, following the equipment's testing procedure. Their readings agreed closely during repeated checks. That reduced support for a persistent difference between the instruments under those conditions. It did not prove that every reading they had ever produced was correct. The comparison also did not establish that the refrigerator had a uniform temperature, because the probes were not being tested in their separate original locations.

The next stage examined position. After the checks, the probes exchanged locations while records were compared at matching times. The higher readings tended to follow the door-side position rather than a particular device. This pattern made location a stronger explanation than a simple fixed error in one thermometer. The technician then compared the temperature records with a log of deliveries and door openings. The differences became larger around periods of repeated access and smaller after the door had remained closed. Together, these observations supported an explanation involving changing conditions within the unit.

Timing still mattered to the staff's earlier impressions. Someone checking a display before a delivery could see a different stage of the cycle from someone checking afterward. A comfortable-looking reading later in the morning did not describe the whole preceding interval. The clinic therefore reviewed recorded histories rather than treating a single observation as a summary of storage. The duration and pattern of a change could matter in ways that its largest displayed value alone did not explain. Records also allowed staff to distinguish a recurring pattern from an isolated observation requiring further investigation.

The investigation led to clearer documentation of probe locations, synchronized times, and checks after equipment was moved. The clinic used an appropriate monitoring arrangement for the stored products rather than assuming that an air measurement at any convenient spot represented their temperature. Staff recorded access events alongside the monitoring history so that future discrepancies could be examined in context. Product-specific storage requirements and professional guidance remained necessary when assessing any possible exposure. The measurement exercise itself was not a test of vaccine effectiveness and could not provide a verdict on a particular batch.

The initial disagreement had offered useful information precisely because the clinic had not erased it by averaging the displays or discarding the warmer reading. Comparing devices together tested one explanation; exchanging their positions tested another; matching records with access times added a third part of the account. None of those steps made monitoring unnecessary. They changed the question from which number should be trusted to what each number described. Reliable control depended on retaining that connection between the measurement, the changing environment, and the decision the measurement was intended to inform.

questions.stem: What conclusion is warranted by the side-by-side comparison?
questions.stem_ja: 二つのセンサーを並べた比較から、どのような結論が正当に導かれるか。

choices.text: The earlier readings could be combined because both devices had now been shown to measure the same time interval.
choices.text_ja: 両方の機器が同じ時間帯を測っていることが示されたので、以前の値をまとめることができた。

choices.text: The storage history was acceptable because neither instrument showed a fixed error during the check.
choices.text_ja: 点検中にどちらの機器にも一定の誤差が見られなかったので、保管の履歴は問題なかった。

choices.text: A persistent difference between the devices became less likely under the tested conditions.
choices.text_ja: 試験した条件のもとでは、機器どうしに一貫した差がある可能性は低くなった。

choices.text: The original refrigerator positions were probably equivalent because both probes behaved similarly.
choices.text_ja: 二つのセンサーが同じように動作したので、冷蔵庫内の元の位置はおそらく同等だった。

questions.stem: Why was exchanging locations informative beyond placing the probes together?
questions.stem_ja: センサーを一緒に置くことに加えて、位置を入れ替えることが有益だったのはなぜか。

choices.text: It demonstrated that the warmer position represented the temperature of every stored product.
choices.text_ja: 温度の高いほうの位置が、保管されているすべての製品の温度を表していることを示したから。

choices.text: It separated deliveries from other door openings without requiring an access log.
choices.text_ja: 開閉の記録がなくても、納品をその他の扉の開閉と区別できたから。

choices.text: It established which device had responded more quickly during the controlled comparison.
choices.text_ja: 管理された比較の間に、どちらの機器がより速く反応したかを立証したから。

choices.text: It showed whether the reading difference followed a device or its position in the unit.
choices.text_ja: 値の差が機器についてまわるのか、冷蔵庫内の位置についてまわるのかを示したから。

questions.stem: How could two careful staff members develop different impressions of the refrigerator’s performance?
questions.stem_ja: 慎重な二人のスタッフが、冷蔵庫の状態について異なる印象を持つことがありえたのはどのようにしてか。

choices.text: Their checks could capture different stages of temperature change around periods of access.
choices.text_ja: 二人の確認が、扉の開閉が続く時間帯の前後で、温度変化の異なる段階をとらえていた可能性があるから。

choices.text: Agreement between same-type probes made position a minor factor, leaving differences in staff judgment as the main explanation.
choices.text_ja: 同じ型のセンサーどうしが一致したので位置は小さな要因となり、スタッフの判断の違いが主な説明として残ったから。

choices.text: The record’s largest value described the whole storage interval better than checks made before and after a delivery.
choices.text_ja: 記録の最大値のほうが、納品の前後に行った確認よりも保管時間全体をよく表していたから。

choices.text: The higher door-side readings identified one device whose earlier calibration had drifted between staff visits.
choices.text_ja: 扉側の高い値から、スタッフの確認の合間に以前の校正がずれていた一方の機器が特定されたから。

questions.stem: Which additional judgment cannot be made from the measurement investigation alone?
questions.stem_ja: 測定の調査だけでは下せない、さらなる判断はどれか。

choices.text: Whether recording access events can help interpret temperature changes.
choices.text_ja: 扉の開閉などの出来事を記録することが、温度変化の解釈に役立つかどうか。

choices.text: Whether a particular vaccine batch remains effective after its storage history.
choices.text_ja: 特定のワクチンのロットが、その保管履歴を経ても有効なままかどうか。

choices.text: Whether probe placement should be documented after monitoring equipment is moved.
choices.text_ja: 監視機器を動かした後に、センサーの設置位置を記録すべきかどうか。

choices.text: Whether a later single reading captures the preceding interval’s full pattern.
choices.text_ja: 後で得られた一回の値が、それ以前の時間のパターン全体をとらえているかどうか。

questions.stem: Why would averaging the initial readings have weakened the investigation?
questions.stem_ja: 最初の値を平均していたら、調査が弱まっていたのはなぜか。

choices.text: The averaged value would reduce random variation enough to make the refrigerator’s position differences less important.
choices.text_ja: 平均した値によって偶然のばらつきが十分に小さくなり、冷蔵庫内の位置による差があまり重要でなくなるから。

choices.text: It would conceal the contrast used to distinguish instrument effects from location and timing effects.
choices.text_ja: 機器による影響を、位置やタイミングによる影響と区別するために使われた違いが見えなくなるから。

choices.text: A common midpoint would provide a storage-wide reference from which each device’s error could be calculated.
choices.text_ja: 共通の中間値が保管庫全体の基準となり、そこから各機器の誤差を計算できるから。

choices.text: Combining the readings would first resolve the disagreement, allowing the access log to explain the remaining variation.
choices.text_ja: 値をまとめることでまず食い違いが解消され、残りのばらつきを開閉の記録で説明できるようになるから。
